notes: Budgets set by the Technical Director, re-baselined to measurement after M3 stage 2 (2026-09-29). Units: raster cycles in this spike, DMA included, which is what the runner measures and what adds up to the 19,656-cycle frame (engine/README.md#budget-units). Framework-style locks (no headroom) only where the path is constant and DMA-free (mux_irq_top); main-loop routines get ~5% over a full-motion-cycle max because their DMA share varies with the sprite layout, not the code. 'stage' is the build stage the engine has reached (docs/milestones/M3-engine-basics.md, rule 1): checks with a higher 'from_stage' print PENDING and fail only under --strict (M3 sign-off). The raster-engineer bumps 'stage' at the start of each stage. Main-loop routines use profile_excl_irq so zone IRQs inside them don't count.

checks.name: mux_sort
checks.source: Measured 2026-09-29, M3 stage 2, 600 passes (a full cycle of the spike's motion, ~480 frames): 479 / 705 / 3,315 min/avg/max (max = the spike reversing three groups of 8 at amp 0). Raster time in the spike, DMA included (engine/README.md#budget-units). The code's CPU cost is flat; the raster spread comes from where badlines and sprite DMA land, so the budget is the 600-pass max + ~5%, rounded up to 50

checks.source: Measured 2026-09-29, M3 stage 2, 600 passes (a full cycle of the spike's motion, ~480 frames): 5,263 / 6,240 / 8,595 (CPU avg ~4,984). Max and average + ~5%. The average is the common case (build rule 3); the max is the sort stress and may stay expensive

checks.source: docs/milestones/M3-engine-basics.md rule 3 as re-baselined after stage 2, and engine/README.md#fast-path: average <= 5,000 raster (about 4,000 CPU; from 6,240) over a full motion cycle, from merging build into select and constant $D01C when uniform. Stays met through stages 3 and 4 in frames with no overflow

checks.name: mux_irq_top (swap + slots 0-7)
checks.source: Measured 378 every pass (stage 2): a constant path in the top border (line 16, no DMA), so this is a lock like the irq_chain budgets. Was 600 (estimate)

checks.name: mux_irq_zone (one IRQ, up to 8 slots)
checks.source: Measured 744 / 962 / 1,500 over 2,000 zone IRQs (stage 2): up to 8 slots at 78 each (DEBUG, no DMA), in-IRQ waits of up to 2 lines per slot, and DMA. + ~6%. A long zone IRQ delays nothing (no fixed entry may sit in the zone region), so this is a regression watch; the costs that matter are the per-frame total and mux_late_count. Was 550 (estimate, 8 x ~60 with no waits or DMA)

checks.name: all IRQ time per frame
checks.source: Measured 2,067-3,562 over 600 frames (stage 2): mux_irq_top 378 + 32, up to 16 zone slots in 2-4 IRQs with waits and DMA, spike_bottom. + ~5%. Raster span, DMA included. Was 3,300 (estimate)

checks.name: free CPU per frame (game promise)
checks.source: engine/README.md#frame-budget: games are promised >= 7,200 cycles a frame for their own logic. In the spike that is spike_move + idle; spike_move is >= 1,907 raster (measured, stage 2), so idle >= 5,300 keeps the promise in every frame, sort stress included. Measured 5,888 (368 x 16) in stage 2. Idle-loop iterations are 16 cycles (counted) and exclude DMA, so this is conservative
